chunks: My father (rah) said: It was narrated to us by Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn 'Amru, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ribat, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A Muslim man continues to be recorded as doing good (as a muhsin) as long as he remains silent; but when he speaks, he is recorded as either doing good or doing evil.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for remaining silent in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq highlights silence as a protective shield against sin, framing it as an active state of worship rather than mere absence of speech. It underscores the principle that speech is a double-edged sword, where the believer's spiritual record shifts from automatic merit to specific judgment based on the content and intent of their words. This concept aligns with the broader ethical emphasis on *hifz al-lisan* (guarding the tongue) as a prerequisite for spiritual refinement.
